lead: Tesla / TSLA — retail can't quit its love
smaller: Oklo / OKLO — nuclear for the data-centre boom
Dogecoin / DOGE — internet jokes as an asset class
why_lead: TSLA is down 28.48% over 20 sessions and 8.64% over five, with a 1-session move of -2.99%, so the drawdown is large enough to be the day's main retail trade. Retail attention on the same day is explicit (CNBC on retail investors not quitting Tesla, Business Insider on owners wanting the CEO back), and the institutional view is split between direction (JPMorgan and the WSJ on valuation, Dan Ives on patience) and pace, which is the cleanest contrast in the day's evidence.
why_smaller: QBTS posted the largest one-session surge in the card (+18.73%, +32.12% over five sessions) on a breakthrough story that retail explicitly chased, but it is a single-name move set against a basket that is down over 20 sessions, so it is a separate narrative from the lead.

OKLO's 20-session drop of 55.96% sits alongside big-tech nuclear pledges and a Stocktwits note that retail sentiment pulled back, which gives a power-demand narrative distinct from both Tesla and quantum.
DOGE's 20-session fall of 31.02% against new memecoin listings and the Trump-linked memecoin drawdown gives the one non-equity trade in the set.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR, -32.17% over 20 sessions): popular in the attention pieces, but the evidence is mostly meme-stock listicles and no single fresh catalyst, so it was not chosen as lead.

Gold and silver (GC=F +2.14% over 20 sessions, record-high headlines): a strong macro story, but the retail attention is thin and it is already covered in the US and Japan blocks and the flows section.
Bitcoin and ether (ETH -29.95% over 20 sessions): the drawdown is large and retail-newcomer headlines exist, but the evidence is mostly analyst technicals, and the crypto section already carries it.
Rocket Lab with 2X ETFs (RKLB -36.39% over 20 sessions, RKLX launched 12 March): product-launch evidence is real, but there is no fresh price-and-attention coincidence beyond meme-stock pieces.
Hims & Hers (HIMS -31.94% over 20 sessions): a court ruling and a GLP-1 scare drove the fall, which is a regulatory story rather than a crowd trade.
Leveraged index ETFs (TQQQ -32.17%, SOXL -34.31% over 20 sessions): the Korean-buyer flow headline is useful, but it is a product story and overlaps the lead's dip-buying theme.
